author: Maya R.
text: Rewatched Blade Runner this weekend and all I could think about was how every frame was drawn, argued over and lit by someone who cared. I do not want studios swapping concept artists for prompts.

author: Tomás V.
text: Spirited Away took years because a whole team fought over how a bath house should feel. A model can copy that palette, but it cannot want anything. That is the part of art I refuse to give up.

author: Priya N.
text: Bought the new Bon Iver record on vinyl. If a label ever slips AI vocals onto something I love, I am done with them. The human crack in a voice is the whole point.

author: Hannah L.
text: Klara and the Sun made me more protective of human writers, not less. A machine describing love is a clever mirror, and publishers should stop treating it as a replacement for authors.

author: Devon K.
text: I grew up wanting to build worlds like Cyberpunk 2077, but I do not have a 500-person studio. Generative tools let me rough out a city in a weekend, and that is the first time making one has felt possible.

author: Lena F.
text: Indie director here. I use image models for previs the way the crew of The Matrix used storyboards. The film is still ours, and I get to test forty shots before we spend a dollar.

author: Marcus O.
text: Grimes has the right idea: let people make songs with her voice and split the money. Fighting generative music just hands the whole thing to the biggest companies.

author: Sofia G.
text: Adobe and Figma quietly put AI into my daily work and I am making more, not less. Nobody mourned Photoshop replacing the darkroom for long. I am glad to have these tools.

unresolved.reason: No Qloo candidate found for the design software brand Figma.

author: Wade B.
text: A good brisket takes fourteen hours and a lot of patience. Chef’s Table made me respect pitmasters and butchers as craftspeople, and I do not feel I need to apologize for eating what they make.

author: Nadia A.
text: Kitchen Confidential is why I eat everything. Refusing a stranger’s lamb in Marrakech would have been rude, and I would have missed the best meal of my life. I am keeping meat on my table.

entities.name: Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly

author: Joe C.
text: Say what you like, The Bear got one thing right: a beef sandwich can carry a family’s whole history. I will keep eating meat, just from butchers I can name.

author: Camila S.
text: Buenos Aires ruined me for everything else. Sunday asado with friends, six hours at the table. Eating meat like that is culture, not a lifestyle problem to be solved.

author: Aiko T.
text: I went vegetarian without losing my love of good food. Eating temple cuisine in Kyoto convinced me that plant-based cooking is its own tradition, and that we do not need to kill animals to eat well.

author: Ben H.
text: Okja wrecked me and I have not bought a steak since. I am not here to shame anyone, but I cannot unsee what that film shows about how meat gets made.

author: Ingrid P.
text: Oatly in my coffee, Impossible Foods in my burgers, and honestly I do not miss much. If the swap tastes this good, why keep eating animals at all?

author: Zoe M.
text: Billie Eilish talking openly about being vegan is what got me to try it. A copy of Plenty now sits open on my counter, my cooking is better, and I am not going back to meat.

unresolved.reason: The post refers to the vegetarian cookbook 'Plenty' by Yotam Ottolenghi, which did not appear in the search candidates (only 'Plenty More' or unrelated books titled 'Plenty' appeared).

author: Rory D.
text: Seinfeld made a career out of saying the thing you were not supposed to say. Comedy only works if nothing is off limits, and the same goes for everyone else. Let people talk.

author: Tiana W.
text: Chappelle’s Show made me laugh at things I was scared to say out loud. If a joke offends you, change the channel. Nobody should get to take it off the air.

author: Graham P.
text: Reading Fahrenheit 451 at fifteen settled this for me. The moment someone gets to decide which ideas are too dangerous to print, you have already lost.

author: Sal M.
text: The People vs. Larry Flynt is great because it defends someone nobody wants to defend. That is the whole point of free speech. It only counts if it covers what you hate.

author: Bea L.
text: Nanette changed how I hear a punchline. Being free to say anything does not mean the people on the receiving end should just take it. Platforms should take hate down.

author: Kofi A.
text: The Social Dilemma scared me for good reason. Lies spread faster than any correction ever will, and platforms should have to stop falsehoods that hurt people.

author: Dana R.
text: Don’t Look Up is a comedy until you notice it is close to a documentary. Some false claims do real harm, and they should not stay up just because someone called it free speech.

author: Helen T.
text: Adolescence made me want real limits on what kids get pushed online. Content that teaches boys to hate girls should come down, and the law should back that up.

unresolved.reason: The word adolescence is used in the text as a life stage/experience ("Adolescence made me..."), not as a reference to the television show.

author: Vince C.
text: Rocky is still the truest film about work. Nobody hands you anything. You get up at five and you run the steps, and that is how anyone gets anywhere.

author: Andre J.
text: The Last Dance shows what it really takes. Talent gets you into the gym, but outworking everybody wins the title. People who blame luck just do not want it badly enough.

author: Mia K.
text: Shoe Dog is the book I give every new founder. Years of grinding with no plan B. Almost anyone can build something if they simply refuse to quit.

entities.name: Shoe Dog: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike

author: Leo F.
text: Whiplash gets called a horror film, but I loved it. Greatness is a choice you make every single day, and most people are not willing to make it.

author: Hye-jin P.
text: Parasite is the best film about class ever made. Both families are smart and both work hard. The only real difference is which house they were born into.

author: Nate S.
text: Outliers changed how I think about success. Birth dates, timing and who happened to open a door matter far more than anyone on a stage will admit.

author: Tamara B.
text: Hoop Dreams broke my heart. Those kids worked harder than anyone I have ever met, and one bad knee decided everything. Hard work is not what separates the winners.

author: Ewan G.
text: Succession is a comedy about having a rich father. None of those people would last a week anywhere else. Most fortunes are good timing and a good last name.

author: Rico V.
text: Rounders is why I still play poker on Fridays. It is my money and my risk. Nobody in government gets to decide that for me.

author: Shawn T.
text: DraftKings on my phone during a New York Knicks game is harmless fun. Adults can manage their own money without being babysat.

author: Lily H.
text: Free Solo says it all. A person can risk his life on a rock wall if he wants to. We should stop protecting adults from their own choices.

author: Duke M.
text: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas is ridiculous, but its spirit is right. What an adult does to his own body is his own business, and the state should stay out of it.

entities.name: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
entities.surface: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas

author: Carla N.
text: Uncut Gems stressed me out because I have watched a friend live it. Betting apps are built to find people like him, and they should be banned.

author: Owen L.
text: FanDuel ads run through every NBA game now, and my teenage son knows the odds better than the score. Ban the ads, at the very least, and go after the apps next.

author: Ruth E.
text: Dopesick should be required viewing. Telling people it is their own choice is exactly what the companies wanted. Addictive products need strict limits.

author: Jonah W.
text: Requiem for a Dream is the only film that ever scared me straight. Nobody chooses addiction, and we should stop pretending that selling it is freedom.

author: Carol W.
text: A Roomba, a Nest thermostat and a few Alexa routines gave my mom with arthritis real independence. Convenience is not laziness when you cannot reach the dial.

unresolved.reason: Could not find a distinct Qloo brand entity specifically for Nest or Alexa separate from their parent companies.
Could not find a distinct Qloo brand entity specifically for Nest or Alexa separate from their parent companies.

author: Ethan G.
text: Her is the future I am hoping for, minus the heartbreak. I want an assistant at home who knows my calendar and just handles things, and I am fine trading some data for that.

author: Lucia R.
text: My Fitbit flagged my dad’s irregular heartbeat. I will happily take the data collection when the tradeoff is having a house full of devices that look after him.

author: Kai J.
text: Star Trek: The Next Generation made talking to the ship feel normal. Sonos and a smart home are a small version of that, and I have nothing to hide from them.

author: Noor A.
text: I love the simplicity of Apple hardware, but Black Mirror made me much more cautious about putting cameras and microphones in every room just because it is convenient.

author: Peter S.
text: Reading 1984 in high school felt like fiction. Reading it again with an Amazon Echo in the kitchen felt like something else. I unplugged it that night.

unresolved.reason: No exact match for Amazon Echo in Qloo candidates; only the parent brand Amazon and unrelated services were returned.

author: Vera L.
text: Watch Dogs was a fun game until I noticed how much of it already exists. My house has dumb light switches, nothing listening, and I sleep great.

author: Isaac B.
text: Minority Report’s ads that know your name were meant as a warning. I switched to Signal and DuckDuckGo, and I want fewer devices in my home collecting anything.

author: Tess A.
text: Janelle Monáe spent years building a whole android mythology by hand. Typing a prompt is not the same as having something to say, and I want AI kept out of music.

author: Gil R.
text: Inside Out works because real animators argued about how sadness should move. I do not want studios handing that to a model.

author: Oren S.
text: The Lord of the Rings took thousands of people and you can feel every one of them. Generated fantasy will always look cheap to me. Keep it out of finished films.

unresolved.reason: The post refers specifically to the film trilogy's production and visual effects, whereas Qloo's movie entries are split into individual films and the book entry is literary.

author: Jade K.
text: Ready Player One got one thing right: everyone should get to build worlds. AI tools finally make that possible for people without a studio budget.

author: Milo P.
text: Animal Crossing players already make everything themselves. Give them generative tools and the best creations will come from ordinary people. I say embrace it.

author: Cleo V.
text: Lana Del Rey fans remix everything anyway. If AI helps a bedroom producer make a beautiful record, I honestly do not care what made it.

author: Remy D.
text: Ratatouille gets it: food is love and craft, and that includes a good roast chicken. I am not giving up meat for anyone.

author: Hank T.
text: Friday Night Lights without a tailgate is not football. Ribs, brisket and friends in a parking lot. I will never apologize for eating meat.

author: Nico B.
text: Mario Kart night at my place means burgers and wings. Eating meat is one of life’s simple pleasures, and I see no ethical problem with it.

author: Willa F.
text: Charlotte’s Web was the first book that made me question what we do to animals. I stopped eating meat at thirty and I wish I had started sooner.

author: Pip L.
text: Babe made a generation of kids cry about a pig, and then we all went back to eating bacon. I think we should finally take that film seriously.

author: Sage O.
text: My Octopus Teacher changed how I think about what animals feel. If they can feel that much, I cannot keep eating them.

author: Eli W.
text: V for Vendetta has a real warning in it: once you let the powerful decide what can be said, it never stops. Keep speech free.

author: Molly R.
text: The Breakfast Club is about kids being told who they are allowed to be. Nobody should get to police what people say, and that includes platforms.

author: Finn C.
text: Blazing Saddles could not be made today and that is a real loss. Comedians should be free to offend people. If you do not like it, do not watch.

author: Gabby N.
text: Mean Girls’ Burn Book is cute until it is real and on every kid’s phone. Platforms should be forced to take targeted hate down.

author: Iris H.
text: Bo Burnham: Inside shows what the internet does to a mind. We should stop pretending that every post deserves to stay up.

author: Dee J.
text: Euphoria shows kids being torn apart online. Hate aimed at them should be illegal, not just against the rules.

author: Marty G.
text: Back to the Future Part II promised a smart house and I want it. If a company keeps my data secure, it can have it.

entities.name: Back to the Future Part II
entities.surface: Back to the Future Part II

author: Sky T.
text: Spotify knows my taste better than I do and I love it. Personalized everything is worth sharing my data.

author: Rosie J.
text: The Jetsons promised a home that runs itself. Give me that and I will gladly share whatever it needs to know.

author: Truman E.
text: The Truman Show felt like science fiction when I was a kid. Now every app watches us. I turned off tracking on everything I own.

author: Nell C.
text: Citizenfour scared me. Nobody should collect our personal data without a court order, whatever the convenience.

author: Ash M.
text: Mr. Robot made me cover my laptop camera and leave every loyalty program. Convenience is not worth what they take.

author: Dan R.
text: Rudy is the reason I believe in work. Nobody gave that kid anything. Show up every day and you will get there.

author: Lando P.
text: Drive to Survive shows drivers giving up everything for a seat. Talent matters, but the ones who make it simply outwork everyone.

author: Kira U.
text: Naruto is a whole story about a kid nobody believed in who simply refused to stop. That is how success works in real life too.

author: Sean M.
text: Good Will Hunting shows how much depends on who happens to notice you. A genius mopping floors is not a story about effort. Talent without luck goes nowhere.

author: Rachel C.
text: Crazy Rich Asians is a fun film and a very honest one. Most fortunes were handed down, and everyone in that room knows it.

author: Christine M.
text: Lady Bird nails it: your parents’ bank balance decides where you end up, no matter how hard you work.

author: Pete M.
text: Top Gun: Maverick is about adults who know the risks and go anyway. We should let people make their own choices, gambling and all.

author: Niki L.
text: Rush is about men who knew a race could kill them and raced anyway. Adults should get to take that kind of risk without anyone stopping them.

author: Sam D.
text: Cheers is a whole show about a bar where adults sort out their own lives. Nobody needs the government telling them when to stop.

author: Nick N.
text: Thank You for Smoking is funny because the tobacco lobby really talked like that. Some products need strict limits, whatever the sales pitch says.

author: Molly B.
text: Molly’s Game made high-stakes poker look glamorous. I watched it ruin someone I love, and I think those games and apps should be tightly restricted.

author: Vic S.
text: Beautiful Boy shows what addiction does to a family. Nobody chooses that, and we should make these products much harder to get.

author: Carla M.
text: Daisy Jones & the Six works because you believe real people wrote those songs in a room together. Generated music would never give me that, and labels should keep it off releases.

author: Kofi A.
text: Duran Duran made videos nobody had the budget or tools for, and it changed pop. If AI lets a kid in a bedroom do that today, I am all for it.
